title: Schengen visa document checklist 2026: your personal list
metaDesc: Documents for a Schengen visa: separate lists for employees, business owners, students, retirees and children. €90 fee, €30,000 insurance, when to apply.
answer: A Schengen visa needs a set of common documents (form, photo, passport, travel insurance with €30,000 cover, bank statements) plus documents that depend on your job and the purpose of your trip. The fee is €90 for adults and €45 for ages 6–12; apply no earlier than 6 months and no later than 15 days before travel.

sections.h: Which country do I apply to?
p: Apply to the consulate (or its official visa centre) of the country where you will spend the most time. If the stays are equal, apply to the country you enter first.

list: Visa fee: €90 for adults, €45 for ages 6–12, free under 6. It is not refunded if refused.
Visa centres (VFS Global, TLScontact, BLS and others) charge an extra service fee.
A decision usually takes 15 days and can be extended to 45 days.
Apply no earlier than 6 months and no later than 15 days before your trip. Book early for summer and holiday periods.

p: Many nationalities can receive longer multiple-entry visas (1, 3 and then 5 years) after using earlier Schengen visas correctly; for Turkish citizens this "cascade" was adopted on 15 July 2025. Always attach copies of your previous visas.

faq.q: How much does a Schengen visa cost?
faq.a: €90 for adults, €45 for children aged 6–12 and free under 6. The visa centre's service fee is extra.

faq.q: What travel insurance do I need?
faq.a: At least €30,000 of medical cover, valid in all Schengen countries for the whole trip.

faq.q: How long does a Schengen visa take?
faq.a: Usually 15 days; it can take up to 45 days if extra checks are needed.

checklist.title: Your personal document list
common: Completed and signed visa application form
2 biometric photos (35×45 mm, white background, taken in the last 6 months)
Passport issued in the last 10 years, valid at least 3 months after you leave, with at least 2 blank pages; copies of previous visas
Copy of your national ID and civil-status documents where required
Travel medical insurance: at least €30,000 cover, valid in all Schengen countries for the whole trip
Bank statements for the last 3 months, stamped or verifiable

statuses.label: Employee
docs: Employer letter with your role, salary and approved leave dates, signed and stamped
Payslips for the last 3 months
Proof of social security / employment record

statuses.label: Business owner / self-employed
docs: Tax registration certificate
Recent certificate of business activity (last 3 months)
Company registration documents and authorised signatures
Company bank statements (if any)

statuses.label: Student
docs: Certificate of enrolment
Sponsorship letter from the person paying for the trip
Sponsor's proof of income and bank statements
Notarised parental consent if you are under 18

statuses.label: Retired
docs: Pension certificate
Pension statements for the last 3 months

statuses.label: Not working / homemaker
docs: Sponsorship letter from the person paying (e.g. your spouse)
Sponsor's employment and income documents
Proof of your relationship (e.g. marriage or family register)

statuses.label: Child under 18
docs: Birth certificate / family register
Notarised consent from any parent not travelling
Copies of both parents' passports or IDs
School enrolment certificate

purposes.label: Tourism
docs: Hotel booking for the whole stay
Short day-by-day itinerary

purposes.label: Visiting family or friends
docs: Invitation letter from your host
Copy of your host's ID or residence permit
Formal guarantee of costs if the country requires it (e.g. Germany's Verpflichtungserklärung)

purposes.label: Business
docs: Invitation letter from the company you are visiting
Letter from your own employer assigning the trip
Meeting, trade fair or training programme

checklist.note: Each consulate may ask for extra documents. Check the current list of the official visa centre before you apply.
